summarized_summary: What you need to be eligable for OAS
personalized_summary: 1. OAS Eligibility: You need to have lived in Canada for at least 40 years after turning 18 to receive the full OAS pension. If you move abroad, you must have lived in Canada for at least 20 years after 18 to qualify for OAS payments outside the country. 2. First Payment: OAS payments start at age 65, but you can choose to delay payments for higher monthly benefits. 3. Taxation: OAS payments are taxable. You don’t need to worry about this now, but be prepared to plan for taxes when you start receiving it. 4. OAS & Residence Abroad: If you plan to travel or live outside Canada in the future, payments will stop if you’re out of the country for more than 6 months and don’t meet residency requirements. 5. Planning Ahead: Start saving and investing for retirement early, as OAS alone may not be sufficient to maintain your lifestyle. Consider other pension plans like CPP or RRSPs.
next_steps: Keep an eye on your eligibility as you build your career and financial future. Consider setting up a My Service Canada Account to monitor your OAS and other government benefits as you approach retirement age.
